Marathon Petroleum is up slightly today as oil prices extended their climb on Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $101 a barrel—the highest since May—after U.S. forces destroyed Iranian oil tankers, raising fears of further supply disruptions from the Persian Gulf. Refineries are running at 98 percent capacity, so higher crude prices flow directly into the company's costs, but the jump in fuel demand concerns and tight supply from geopolitical risk has supported energy sector valuations broadly.

The two-week rally of 12.5 percent reflects the sharp run-up in oil prices over the same window, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict. With Brent now above $101 and U.S. crude at $91.50, refining margins remain supported by the supply uncertainty, even as storage levels remain elevated—refineries are already operating at near-maximum rates, limiting their ability to capture additional margin from price spikes.
